ai.summary: Roving-tabindex tabs: the tablist owns the keyboard, arrows move and activate, and the active panel is the only one rendered.
whenToUse: Related content shares one surface and only one view matters at a time
The views are peers — Settings-style sections, editor panes
Switching should feel like moving, not navigating
whenNotToUse: Each view is a destination — use navigation, not tabs
The views must be compared side by side — show them all
Content must stay mounted across switches — this component unmounts inactive panels
ai.accessibility: The ARIA tabs pattern's hard rule is enforced: only the active tab is in the tab order, arrow keys move and activate (automatic activation), Home and End jump to the ends, and activation wraps. Tabs are real `<button>`s. `aria-selected` / `aria-controls` / `aria-labelledby` are computed and written by the widget, because tabs and panels are separately slotted. Arrow semantics derive from `getComputedStyle().direction` at interaction time, so `dir="rtl"` inverts Left and Right with no build flag (§4). The active panel carries `tabindex=0` so keyboard users reach its content after the last tab.

Account settings.

Billing history.
knownLimitations: Inactive panels are hidden, not kept alive — state inside a panel is lost on switch, unless the application holds it
The tablist slot must carry `data-slot="tablist"` and each part its `data-slot` — the wiring contract is structural
